section.heading: Prohibition on certain medical lending promotion.

para.text: For the purposes of this section, the term "medical lending product" shall have the same meaning as provided in [§ 44-423(6)].
A health care provider, as that term is defined in § 28-3814(dd)(7)(B), shall not:
Complete, or assist a patient in completing, any portion of an application for a medical lending product;
Promote a medical lending product to a patient who:
Is under the influence of general anesthesia, conscious sedation, or moderation sedation, including any period in which the patient has been advised not to engage in activities due to such influence;
Is in a treatment area, including an exam room, surgical room, or other area where medical treatment is administered, unless an area separated from the treatment area does not exist on site;
Charge a medical lending product for a medical procedure before the date of the procedure or before costs have been incurred;
Charge a medical lending product or another form of credit when the patient's insurance, including Medicaid, will cover the services, unless the amount is for a copay, deductible, or co-insurance;
Require credit card pre-authorization or require the patient to have a credit card on file prior to administering emergency health services; or

If the services were provided at a health care facility-FAP, as defined in § 44-401(10A), offer a medical lending product or another form of credit until the health care facility-FAP has offered or conducted a financial assistance eligibility screening pursuant to [§ 44-425].

section.codify:annotation: Applicability of D.C. Law 26-172: § 6 of D.C. Law 26-172 provided that the creation of this section by § 3(a)(2) of D.C. Law 26-172 is subject to the inclusion of the law’s fiscal effect in an approved budget and financial plan. Therefore that amendment has not been implemented.
